$comment: Shared contract between app/ordering.py:display_key (server) and frontend/src/lib/order.ts:columnComparator (client). Both sort the same case with their own implementation and must produce `expected_ids`. Consumed by backend/tests/test_ordering_contract.py and frontend/src/lib/order.contract.test.ts — neither owns it.
why: A drag sends an ANCHOR ('put it before #42'), never a position. The client picks that anchor from what the user SEES, the server inserts into what it STORES, so the two orderings have to be the same one. While they drifted apart, a drag was saved and still changed nothing on screen — indistinguishable from 'reordering is broken'. A prose note asking the next person to keep both sides in step cannot fail; this can.
fields: Only stored fields may take part, and every rule has to be one the USER can override — a rule they cannot (ordering by execution time) turns their drag into a no-op. Priority bands the queue and is allowed for exactly that reason: dragging across a band bounces back, but raising the priority always gets the card where they want it.

cases.name: drag order decides
cases.why: The default case: nothing special about these, so sort_order alone rules.

cases.name: equal sort_order breaks by id
cases.why: The order has to be TOTAL. Ties left undecided would let two clients disagree, and the renumbering after a move would then depend on which row the database happened to return first.

cases.name: blocked sinks to the bottom
cases.why: Even with the lowest sort_order — blocked is the first key.

cases.name: blocked prompts keep their own order among themselves
cases.why: Sinking them must not shuffle them; the queue stays predictable.

cases.name: tested sinks below untested in done
cases.why: What is finished and checked moves out of the way of what still needs checking.

cases.name: tested is meaningless outside done
cases.why: The flag only exists for finished work; in the queue it must not move anything.

cases.name: tested prompts follow the drag order among themselves
cases.why: They were once ordered by execution time, which put a dragged card straight back where it came from — the move was saved and looked like it was not.

cases.name: blocked outranks tested
cases.why: A blocked prompt goes to the very bottom whatever else is true of it.

cases.name: all three rules at once
cases.why: The realistic shape of a done column: untested by drag order, then tested by drag order, then blocked last.

cases.name: negative and zero sort_order are ordinary values
cases.why: A prompt moved to the top of DONE gets min-1, which goes negative as soon as the column starts at 0.

cases.name: high priority leads the queue
cases.why: The whole point of the field: urgent work is what you see first, whatever was dragged where.

cases.name: the drag order still decides inside a band
cases.why: Priority groups the column, it does not replace the manual order — otherwise raising a priority would throw away every drag in that band.

cases.name: priority is meaningless outside the queue
cases.why: Urgency answers 'what next', a question only the queue asks. A finished prompt that happened to be urgent must not shuffle the Done column.

cases.name: blocked outranks priority
cases.why: Blocked work is parked, however urgent it was — it sinks even past a low-priority prompt.

cases.name: a missing priority reads as normal
cases.why: Rows written before the field existed must sort exactly where they did before, or the migration silently reshuffles the board.

cases.name: genau-testen leads the done column
cases.why: Done is where 'what still needs checking' is asked, so the prompts marked for a thorough test come first — whatever was dragged where.

cases.name: being tested outranks genau-testen
cases.why: A marked prompt that has ALREADY been tested must not climb over the untested ones — it would leave the folded block and land back in the part that means 'still to do', after the careful look it asked for has happened.

cases.name: genau-testen does nothing outside done
cases.why: The flag survives a status change but is only a note elsewhere; a queued prompt carrying it must keep its dragged position.
